newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK SETS BID CONDITIONS FOR AGROBANKA SALE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK SETS BID CONDITIONS FOR AGROBANKA SALE.

text.p: The Czech central bank set the minimum bid for "sound assets" in Agrobanka a.s. at "around" four billion crowns and the deadline for the first round of bids for May 16, the bank's forced administrator said on Wednesday.
"We accept the minium price for this good part of Agrobanka at around this level (four billion crowns)," said Jiri Klumpar Agrobanka's forced administrator.
Last month the central bank said it had divided Agrobanka's assets into "sound" and "questionable" portions. It said it would sell the sound assets to a strategic investor.
Klumpar said that around 100 potential investors had expressed an interest. "There are more interested investors than I had expected," he said.
He added that he hoped the sell off process would be completed by the end of July.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) had originally said it would be interested in taking up to a 20 percent stake in Agrobanka.

But Klumpar said that the EBRD would step back from taking a stake if a strong enough strategic investor could be found who would be willing to buy 100 percent of Agrobanka's assets being offered for sale.
